items_missed: No agenda statement — opened with 'seeing you had a few moments to go over the information' but never laid out the roadmap (gather details, then pricing) or the 10-15 minute timeframe, and never asked 'sound good?'
Never asked about packing services at all, on a one-bedroom move with 15-25 boxes where packing was a live upsell
Never asked about additional stops or storage stops — notable since the customer volunteered he is already shuttling loads to the new place himself
Never asked about garage, storage unit, or balcony contents at the origin apartment
No 'no hidden fees' pitch — said 'everything is included' but never named no credit card fees, no transportation fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees
Referenced 'once we go over that minimum' without ever stating the 2.5-hour minimum, so the customer heard a rule he was never given
No sense-check after the Save Your Ass prep speech — 'Does that make sense?' came earlier after the clock explanation, not after the prep coaching
Never said 'no deposit required' — one of Einstein's two headline differentiators, and it went unmentioned
Did not explain the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email or ask the customer to reply with corrections — only offered reply-to-email as a contact channel
Did not give hours of operation when explaining how to reach the team
Used the customer's name only twice ('may I speak with Anthony', 'Thanks Anthony') — short of the 3+ bar
Insurance explanation covered No Worries $2,000 but omitted the 60 cents/lb baseline that makes the coverage land as a differentiator

Audible fumbling reading the quote form back — 'moving from 650 square foot floor, a square foot. Oh, my gosh, I do apologize. That's like is it Friday one bedroom' — undercut an otherwise clean recap
top_strength: The estimate work was the best part of this call and it is exactly what the estimate-accuracy rock needs. The system quoted three hours; Bri heard the two-landing staircase, said 'the system quoted you about three hours with those stairs I would like to probably do between 3:00 and four just to kind of allow time for them to manage like you said the stairs,' and then confirmed the adjustment with the customer. She also captured the 20-foot walk from parking to stairs, offered to pad and wrap the 70-inch TV off to the side, and covered all three differentiators plus disassembly/reassembly of the bed. Rapport was genuinely good — the puppy and farm exchange, 'just let her run free,' and 'getting out, isn't that always the case?' had the customer laughing and thanking her for reaching out.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix: open with a real agenda. Sixty seconds of 'Anthony, here's how this will go — I'll gather a few details about your move, then walk you through pricing and what to expect on move day. Takes about 10 to 15 minutes. Sound good?' costs nothing and buys permission to run the whole checklist, which is why the packing, storage, and additional-stops questions all got skipped here. Second priority: finish the pricing block. 'Everything is included' is not the pitch — name it: no credit card fees, no transportation fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees, and no deposit to hold the date. The no-deposit line is a booking-confidence lever and it never got said. Third, close the prep speech with a sense-check — the prep coaching itself was strong and the customer was already volunteering to take carloads over, so ask 'does that make sense?' and let him commit out loud. Last, small thing with real weight: use Anthony's name three or four times through the middle of the call, not just at hello and goodbye.
phone_presence_notes: Real two-way rapport — the dog and farm exchange, the gravity joke, and the customer closing with 'I appreciate you reaching out' — held back from a 5 by name use only twice and some stumbling while reading the quote form.
